recommended.name: RF + EMS + LED Neck & Jaw Sculpting Device
recommended.positioning: Below-the-chin skin tightening. Not a face device.
recommended.pain: Sagging jawline, jowls and crepey neck skin. The neck is the age tell people cannot hide with makeup. Clinical alternatives are a neck lift ($7k-15k) or Ultherapy ($2k-4k), so the willingness to pay $89 is already established.
recommended.evergreen_evidence: RF is the structural growth leader in home beauty devices: 18.7% CAGR, 30%+ of category share, 42% of consumers name it their primary interest. Home-use beauty devices $14.4B (2026) to $21.85B (2030), 11% CAGR. Anti-aging is evergreen by construction, not a fad cycle.

upsells.name: RF conductive gel (4oz)
upsells.note: Device does not conduct or glide without it. Mandatory consumable = built-in repeat purchase.

recommended.saturation_note: Category is validated but the ANGLE is open. LED face masks, pore vacuums and ice rollers are explicitly the saturated plays. Verified incumbent pricing (Aug 2026): NuFACE Trinity starter $350 (complete $525), TriPollar STOP Vx $629, STOP Vx Gold $849. Nothing credible sits under $100, so an $89 offer enters an empty price band rather than undercutting a crowded one. Below-the-chin devices are named as the 2026 expansion area rather than a crowded one.
recommended.verdict_notes: Buy at or under $26 to keep the 3x gate safe. At a $32 supplier cost, $89 falls to 2.78x markup and fails gate 2 even though net profit is still $30.30.
pain_review_language: Finally an easy to use and comfortable device to address aging skin.
got rid of my second chin and sagging skin on my jawline
I will never stop using this. My skin is tighter, firmer and glowing.

unverified.meta_ads_library: Not reachable. /ads/library/ returns 403 to non-browser clients and keyword search needs a logged-in FB session. TikTok Creative Center also login-gated. No competitor ad spend or run-length is measured or claimed.
unverified.supplier_cost: $24 is a published wholesale range, not a confirmed SKU quote.
unverified.google_trends: Evergreen case rests on market CAGR data, not a pulled 5-year Trends curve.

runner_up.name: Microcurrent Facial Toning Device
runner_up.pain: Loss of facial definition and muscle tone.
runner_up.evergreen_evidence: Unit sales +22.4%, market $691M (2025), but a slower 7% CAGR and visible Dec/Jan gifting peaks with a May trough.
runner_up.saturation_note: Weaker on gate 6 than the RF pick. NuFACE has trained the market so hard that most listings read as dupes, and search interest is seasonal rather than flat.
runner_up.verdict_notes: Passes all six gates but on thinner ground. Hold as the second test, not the first.

rejected.name: LED Face Mask
rejected.reason: Gate 6. Highest-share device sub-category (23.7% of facial device market, +27.6% YoY) and named across dropshipping roundups as a top pick, which is exactly the problem. Competing against Omnilux, CurrentBody and Shark plus every dropshipper running the same creative.

rejected.name: Ice Roller / Cryo Globes
rejected.reason: Gates 2 and 6. Supplier cost around $3-5 forces a 7x+ markup to reach $20 net, which the perceived value will not carry. Market described as competitive with many brands selling variants.

rejected.name: Blackhead / Pore Vacuum
rejected.reason: Gate 1 and 6. Pain is cosmetic-mild rather than deep, the device underdelivers against the satisfying-content marketing that sells it, and the resulting refund rate blows past the 5% returns assumption in the formula.

rejected.name: Facial Steamer
rejected.reason: Gate 3. Bulky and water-holding, pushing shipping past the $5 ceiling.

rejected.name: Microneedling / derma pen
rejected.reason: Gate 2 in practice, via ad policy. The economics look excellent ($22 cost, $79 sell, $33.30 net, and mandatory single-use cartridges are the best repeat-purchase profile in skincare) but Meta bans any image or video showing needles penetrating skin, and lists microneedling among restricted cosmetic procedures. You cannot show the product working. With ad spend at 20% of revenue, a product whose core demo is unadvertisable breaks the formula's central assumption.

rejected.name: Under-eye / microcurrent eye massager wand
rejected.reason: Gate 6. Strong pain and clean economics, but it is already a commodity dropship SKU: stocked as a category on Doba, listed across viral-beauty-gadget roundups for 2026, and dense with near-identical Amazon listings. Eye Massage Machine market also grows slower than the alternatives at 6.8% CAGR. Right pain, wrong moment.

additional.name: Red Light Scalp & Hair Density Comb
additional.positioning: Scalp-as-skincare. Sold on thinning density and part-width, not 'hair loss cure'.
additional.pain: Visible scalp through the part, widening hairline, thinning density. Among the deepest confidence pains in personal care, checked in the mirror daily. Clinical alternatives run to transplants at $4k-15k or lifelong finasteride, so a $99 device is the cheap option in the consideration set.
additional.evergreen_evidence: Scalp category up 19% YoY (Circana, H1 2025). Hair growth devices $1.8B (2025) to $4.1B (2034) at 9.4% CAGR; the LED sub-segment holds 37.4% share and grew 31% YoY to $1.4B. 'Skinification of the scalp' is the named 2026 trend, which is what makes this a skincare product rather than a haircare one.

upsells.name: Peptide scalp density serum
upsells.note: Stacks with the device and is the protocol most competitors sell alongside it.

additional.saturation_note: Validated by a 31% YoY LED sub-segment, and the incumbents are caps and helmets at $200-800 (Kiierr, HairMax, iRestore, CurrentBody). A $99 comb is a different form factor at a different price. Notably absent from the viral-dropship-gadget roundups that list LED masks, ice rollers and eye massagers, which is the gate 6 signal worth having.
additional.verdict_notes: Buy at or under $33 to hold 3x at $99. Frame as density and scalp health; medical regrowth claims are what draw ad review.

additional.name: Blue + Red Light Acne Spot Treatment Device
additional.positioning: Targeted spot wand, deliberately not the LED mask form factor.
additional.pain: Inflammatory and cystic breakouts. Acne reshapes whether people leave the house, and the emotional load is disproportionate to the physical symptom. Buyers already spend on prescriptions, derm visits and a rotating shelf of failed products.
additional.evergreen_evidence: Acne treatment devices $7.18B (2025) to $7.61B (2026) at 6.0% CAGR, reaching $9.54B by 2030. Acne light therapy units 25-35M (2026) to 55-75M (2035), 7-10% CAGR. Acne is structurally evergreen and skews to a continuously replenishing younger cohort.

upsells.name: Hydrocolloid pimple patches (60ct)
upsells.note: Highest repeat rate of any upsell in this portfolio - genuinely consumable.

additional.saturation_note: The category is FDA-cleared and proven (Solawave Bye Acne, Omnilux Clear, DRx SpectraLite), which is validation. The saturated form factor is the MASK - dropship sources report buying acne masks near $30 and selling $80-100, with saturation rated roughly 7/10. The spot wand is the same technology in the uncrowded shape.
additional.verdict_notes: At a $16 cost this sits BELOW the $18.18 crossover, so the $20 net rule binds, not 3x: the floor is $51.43, not $48. Only $7.57 of headroom at $59 - the tightest of the three. Ad creative is the real constraint: Meta rejects close-up problem-area imagery and insecurity-based copy, so lead with the clear-skin outcome, never the breakout.
